messages:
sam_support: Heads-up — ACME (acme-corp) opened an escalation. p95 TTFB for our SSE streaming endpoint jumped from ~180ms to ~1.4s across last 48h. Non-streaming endpoints look fine.
acme_ops: Confirmed. Only /v1/stream/generate (SSE) affected. Attached minimal repro timings from their client — we see initial chunk delayed but total tokens stream at normal rate after first chunk.
acme_ops: curl timings snippet:
  time_namelookup: 0.005
  time_connect: 0.060
  time_starttransfer(TTFB): 1.420
  time_total: 3.120
They also said toggling to non-stream gives TTFB ~0.17s and time_total ~3.2s (so total same, streaming first-byte much worse).
sam_support: @jin_runtime can you take a look? customer is on Dedicated reserved pool (us-east-1). Tenant id: acme-corp-24.
jin_runtime: ok — quick Qs: any recent rollout to edge proxy or coalescing changes last 72h? Also need model + quantization variant and sequence length distribution.
lina_cs: ACME on model redwood/gpt-medium-v2-quant, avg prompt tokens 60, response tokens ~220.
mira_sre: We had an edge proxy tweak 36h ago to increase HTTP/2 flush coalescing window (to reduce qps pressure). Could be related.
edge-bot: deploy: edge-proxy v2.14.3 rolled to us-east-1 at 4781948000 (coalesce-window: 200ms -> 350ms), rolling canary -> full.
jin_runtime: that aligns. For SSE we rely on small immediate flushes: coalesce-window increase would delay first chunk until buffer fills or timer fires. Non-stream path buffers until end-of-chunk so TTFB different behavior.
jin_runtime: repro steps I want to run:
  1) curl -N --header "Accept: text/event-stream" -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream/generate
  2) compare with same request but non-streaming endpoint
  3) capture edge-proxy logs: request_id, flush timers, chunk sizes
mira_sre: I'll pull proxy traces and check flush timers for acme-corp tenant. Also verify whether dedicated pool route uses same edge config or special handling.
jin_runtime: quick mitigation options while we investigate:
  - temporarily set edge coalesce-window for acme-corp to 50ms (tenant override)
  - or route their traffic to non-streaming endpoint fallback (maintains UX but removes streaming interactivity)
  - tweak runtime to emit an immediate small first chunk (heartbeat chunk) before main content
lina_cs: customer prefers to keep streaming UX. They asked for minimal disruption, so tenant override for coalesce-window is best if low-risk.
mira_sre: Can do tenant-scoped flag. Pushing a tenant override is low-risk and reversible. I'll open an ops change at low traffic hours.
alex_prod: Also check if model variant changed autoscaling patterns — small KV cache priming could increase first-token compute if cache misses more often.
jin_runtime: good call. I'll check KV cache hit rates for acme-corp on that model across the last 72h.
acme_ops: we can provide a sample request_id from their client: req-2026031521-ACME-9f7. They observed a couple hundred customer sessions with similar TTFB spike.
jin_runtime: thanks — grabbing logs for req-2026031521-ACME-9f7 now. Initial look: edge shows delayed flush timer firing at ~1.3s, runtime received request at ~60ms and started generating, first kv-cache-dependent token compute appears fast. So edge coalescing looks like culprit.
sam_support: plan summary?
jin_runtime: 1) Mira will push tenant override to reduce coalesce-window to 50ms for acme-corp (canary 1% -> 100% if green) 2) I will validate KV cache hit rates and confirm no runtime regression 3) Lina will inform customer and offer fallback non-stream if they want immediate option 4) if tenant override helps, we schedule edge-proxy config rollback or refinement to avoid global perf hit
mira_sre: change request created: CHG-32489. Canaries start in 10m and full rollout in 30m if no errors. I'll post results.
edge-bot: change CHG-32489: tenant-coalesce-override(acme-corp)->50ms initiated by mira_sre at 4782010200
mira_sre: Canary metrics: p95 TTFB for acme-corp dropped from 1.42s -> 0.19s during 1% canary window. No error spike. Rolling to 100% now.
sam_support: amazing — customer replied: "seeing streaming feel snappier, thanks". They want postmortem and permanent fix options.
jin_runtime: next steps for root cause: 1) revert global coalesce-window bump or make it tenant-adaptive 2) consider runtime-first-chunk heartbeat so clients get immediate first-byte even with proxy coalescing 3) instrument more explicit metrics: per-tenant edge flush wait-time and pre-kv-cache compute delay
alex_prod: agree. Also add automated alert if per-tenant TTFB delta between streaming and non-streaming exceeds threshold.
lina_cs: I'll schedule customer follow-up and share timeline/PM notes. Customer wants a short RCA and mitigation timeline by EOD.
sam_support: I'll open support ticket SUP-68231 and add these action items. Closing loop once RCA doc is ready.
